quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When the sun is shining.
When you think stopping will be easy.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Increase your following distance in these situations.

questions.question: How do you make a quick turn on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Lean the motorcycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the motorcycle quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, lean your motorcycle in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: What happens if your rear wheel locks while stopping in a straight line?

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to get control back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can best manage road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can best manage road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. Adjust your position as needed.

questions.question: What should you do if you get a flat tire while riding?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and do not use the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly and stay in a straight line. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Leave the road once your motorcycle has slowed down.

questions.question: When should you keep a longer following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through the vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Keep at least a four-second following distance in these situations.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: How should you cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Use the shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight through your lane when crossing angled railroad tracks. Changing your angle may push you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you complete a turn or lane change. Leaving it on after moving confuses other drivers about your next action.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.
No, but it is recommended.
Only for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog chases your motorcycle?

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and leave it behind.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If chased, slow down and downshift. Let the dog approach. Then accelerate quickly to leave it behind.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle handle turns when carrying a passenger?

options.text: It responds more slowly than usual.
It responds more quickly than usual.
It responds normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: It responds more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond to turns, speed changes, and stops.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger before riding?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid talking or moving unnecessarily while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking or moving unnecessarily while riding.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible, not far back.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When you will be slowing down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as bright as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others notice you are decelerating. This is especially important for sudden stops.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be positioned in a group?

options.text: At the very front leading the group.
Near the front of the group, behind the leader.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group, behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Place less experienced riders near the front of the group behind the leader. Experienced riders can then lead the way and watch the inexperienced riders.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: How should you brake when making a normal stop on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both the front and rear brakes together. Also downshift at the same time.

questions.question: What should passengers do when you take a turn or curve?

options.text: Look over their shoulder in the direction of the turn.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and the bike lean in the correct direction.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is considered intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are intoxicated. You cannot legally drive if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a helmet protect you?

options.text: U.S. DOT-compliant.
Loose-fitting.
Free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fit snugly all the way around your head, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. A loose helmet does not protect you well.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move to the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane that puts you in another driver's field of vision as early as possible.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: Not until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
